title: Why Your Roof Isn't Just Flat Boards
sources: IKO 'Why is there ponding water on my flat roof?' / ARMA 'Ponding water basics' / Wikipedia 'Ponding': water that sits on a flat or poorly drained roof causes leaks and decay, so roofs are sloped to drain

InterNACHI 'Collar & rafter ties' / ICC 'Rafter and ceiling joist framing' / Fine Homebuilding 'Keeping cathedral-ceiling walls from bowing': loaded rafters push the tops of the walls outward; rafter ties / ceiling joists across the bottom hold them together

Fine Homebuilding 'Introduction to Roof Trusses' / Make: 'How do trusses work?' / Hunker 'Why are triangles used in trusses': a triangle cannot change shape without changing the length of a side, so trusses are built from triangles

IRC R905.2.1 (solidly sheathed deck) and R905.1.1 (underlayment) as quoted by Minnesota Rule 1309.0905 / Grand Rapids MI 'Roof assembly requirements' / Sioux Falls 'Asphalt shingles': asphalt shingles go on a solid deck (plywood/OSB) over underlayment

IRC R905.2.6 (jaspector.com) / Asphalt Roofing Manufacturers Association 'Nail application of asphalt strip shingles': not less than four fasteners per strip shingle (six in some high-wind cases); courses overlap so water runs over the shingle below

University of Minnesota Extension 'What is an ice dam?' / PNNL Building America Solution Center 'Ice dam prevention' / UMass 'Preventing ice dams' / NWS Grand Rapids: heat from the house melts roof snow, it refreezes at the cold eave into an ice dam and water backs up under the shingles; air sealing, insulation and soffit + ridge ventilation keep the roof deck cold
IRC R806.2 (jaspector.com 'IRC 2024 attic ventilation 1-to-150') : ventilated attics with intake vents low (soffit) and exhaust high (ridge)

lines.text: If you lay flat boards across your walls, the first rain turns your house into a bathtub.
lines.caps: If you lay *flat boards | across your *walls, | the first *rain turns your house | into a *bathtub.

lines.text: So you tilt them into a slope, and the rain runs off.
lines.caps: So you *tilt them | into a *slope, | and the rain runs *off.

lines.text: But those sloped rafters push outward, and your walls start to lean.
lines.caps: But those sloped *rafters | push *outward, | and your walls start to *lean.

lines.text: So you tie the bottoms with one more board, making a triangle that can't change shape.
lines.caps: So you *tie the bottoms | with one more *board, | making a *triangle | that can't change *shape.

lines.text: But then rain pours through the gaps between them.
lines.caps: But then *rain pours | through the *gaps between them.

lines.text: So you nail sheets of plywood across the top.
lines.caps: So you nail *sheets | of *plywood across the top.

lines.text: But wood soaks up water and rots.
So you roll out a waterproof layer,
then shingles in rows that overlap like fish scales.
lines.caps: then *shingles in rows | that *overlap | like *fish scales.

lines.text: Each one gets at least four nails.
But in winter, your warm house melts the snow,
lines.caps: But in *winter, | your *warm house | melts the *snow,

lines.text: it refreezes at the edge, and the water backs up under your shingles.
lines.caps: it *refreezes at the edge, | and the *water backs up | under your *shingles.

lines.text: So you cut vents at the edge and the top, and cold air keeps the roof cold.
lines.caps: So you cut *vents | at the edge and the *top, | and cold *air | keeps the roof *cold.

lines.text: Slope, triangles, plywood, shingles, vents, and you've just built a roof.
lines.caps: *Slope, triangles, | *plywood, shingles, | *vents, | and you've just built a *roof.
